correctness.rationale: For positive t, the differentiated integrands of H are bounded locally in t even for unbounded K; at t=0 the first moment suffices. H'(0+)=γ−μ<0, H''>0, and there is an ε>0 with positive mass on K≤γ−ε, forcing divergence of H. The unique minimum c*=H(t*) is in (0,1). The exact ratio (1−F(v))/(1−v)=H(t) gives a global supporting line with just the two contacts v* and 1. Up to v* the derivative F'=H−H'/γ decreases strictly from μ/γ to c*, so the joined curve is the least concave majorant and optimizing over the entire closed interval gives all four regimes, including the two-maximizer c=c* case and the unique zero optimizer at c=μ/γ. The positive-time return of H to 1 proves the unique surplus crossing. For the witness, e^(t*/2)=√3; the partial slope equation is q+9/q=8c with q=e^(t/2) in (1,√3), confirming the smaller root, crossing v=8/9, and both partial-branch limits.
residual_risks: Finite-mixture grids are not an arbitrary-law proof. The claim needs positive rates almost surely (for F(1)=1), the moment and slow-mass inequalities, and the asymptotic full event.

value.rationale: The problem asks whether increasing a per-volume cost favors less of a storm gradually or produces a discontinuous full-to-partial switch. The unique cost tie, complete branch and crossing formulas are useful as an exact benchmark for heterogeneous first-flush design heuristics. They are not just application of an envelope to a known empirical curve: the result identifies precisely the contacts and strict branch structure for every admissible initial-stock law.
residual_risks: No field-performance, finite-duration event, nonlinear cost or interevent operations conclusion follows.
